currentContext.expansion: As an asset-light IT services company, expansion is primarily delivery-footprint and inorganic rather than physical capacity build-out. The Company continued its programmatic M&A-led expansion strategy (overseen by a two-Executive-Director Investment Committee), building on a history of acquisitions — Cupola (09 May 2017, IoT CoE), OSS Cube (29 May 2017, digital/open-source, North America presence), Happiest Minds Inc. risks.risk: Revenue concentration in international markets and foreign-exchange exposure
risks.note: The ERM chapter's Key Risks table leads with this: dependence on international revenues exposes the Company to adverse foreign currency movements, causing potential volatility in revenues and margins. Managed by a natural hedge (offsetting FX inflows against outflows) plus plain-vanilla forward contracts of up to one year maturity laid out in a laddered format against forecast inflows, all overseen by the Board's Risk Management Committee; the Company also reports constant-currency revenue growth to give a currency-neutral view.

risks.risk: Customer credit - delay or default in client payments
risks.note: Flagged under Financial Risks as capable of hitting cash flows, lengthening receivable days and impairing working capital efficiency. The Company's own quantification of the containment is debtor days of 94 as of March 31, 2026, supported by short billing and collection cycles, periodic reassessment of customer creditworthiness, credit limits and enforcement of contractual payment terms.

risks.risk: Availability of credit and liquidity management
risks.note: The AR states that inadequate liquidity may restrict the Company's ability to meet its financial obligations and support business operations. Mitigation rests on proactive monitoring of liquidity positions, diverse banking relationships under multiple banking arrangements, and maintaining access to undrawn borrowing facilities and other credit lines for short- and long-term needs; the Board's Report also confirms the Company is continuing a programmatic M&A agenda across the US, Europe and the Middle East, which keeps funding capacity a live constraint.

risks.risk: Financial performance falling short of stated guidance
risks.note: Uniquely for an Indian AR, management lists guidance-miss itself as a risk: variance between actual performance and planned guidance may impact investor confidence and market perception. The control is analytical plan-building, monthly monitoring of financial performance against plan, and using each team's submitted guidance to track performance and trigger interventions.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity and data privacy, specifically ransomware and malware
risks.note: BRSR material issue No. 5, classified R,O, names the risk as the ransomware/malware threat, with negative financial implications spelt out as operational disruptions, data breaches and significant financial and reputational damage. Controls are described as robust prevention and containment of malware spread across the IT environment and critical applications, alongside a defined employee notification process for data subject rights. Structural for a company that sells cybersecurity services through IMSS - a breach is both an operating loss and a credibility loss in a revenue line.

risks.risk: Business capability and resilience - loss of data or impact to business and functions
risks.note: BRSR material issue No. 7, classified as a pure risk (R). The Company concedes that although it follows a mature business resilience framework, periodic testing is needed to stay aligned with evolving business and security expectations, and runs regular security incident simulations and tabletop exercises. Stated downside of failing to address systemic risk effectively is data loss or disruption of critical business functions leading to financial losses, regulatory penalties and erosion of stakeholder trust.

risks.risk: Brand positioning and market differentiation in an AI-led services market
risks.note: The only Business Risk (as opposed to Financial Risk) reproduced in the ERM table: with industry focus shifting towards AI, the Company says it is important that it brands itself accordingly. Response was to reposition the organisation as an AI-first organisation to sharpen the GTM narrative around AI-led transformation, engineering excellence and industry depth, plus investment in thought leadership, client success stories and analyst engagement. This is a differentiation risk for a mid-cap competing against far larger AI-first narratives.

Named as a material topic under the Social pillar in the Company's own materiality assessment, and the risk is sharpened by the MD&A FY27 outlook, which expects hiring across the industry to remain selective with emphasis on skill transformation, specialised digital capabilities and workforce productivity rather than broad-based headcount expansion. For a people-led digital engineering business, the ability to reskill the existing base rather than hire ahead is the operating variable.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's IT/ITeS industry enters FY27 at a strategic inflection point, transitioning from scale-led growth toward value-driven, AI-centric transformation, after demonstrating resilience in FY26 amid global macroeconomic uncertainty and cautious discretionary spending
- As per NASSCOM estimates, India's technology industry is expected to have crossed USD 315 billion in revenue by FY26, with an increasing share of growth driven by AI-led transformation, digital engineering and platform-centric services
- Overall technology spending expected to remain measured at 5-7% YoY entering FY27, while enterprise AI investment continues to scale progressively from experimentation toward organization-wide deployment
- FY27 expected to see the industrialisation of Generative AI and Agentic AI as enterprises move beyond pilot programs to embed AI into core processes, driving demand for higher-value consulting, engineering, integration and managed services beyond traditional effort-based delivery models
- Digital Engineering and ER&D expected to remain structurally strong growth areas, with India strengthening its position as a global ER&D hub via a deep engineering talent base and expanding Global Capability Centers
- The cloud, data and AI infrastructure investment cycle expected to remain a key growth driver; cybersecurity and digital trust emerging as board-level priorities as AI adoption raises enterprise risk exposure and regulatory scrutiny
- Operating model expected to continue shifting toward outcome-based engagement models, IP-led solutions and platform monetisation; hiring trends likely to stay selective, emphasizing skill transformation and workforce productivity over broad-based headcount expansion

- [Wage code] An exceptional item described as "New wage code cost" appears in FY26 (₹1,859 lakhs) with quarterly entries of ₹2,203 lakhs in Q3 FY26 and ₹(344) lakhs in Q4 FY26; nil in Q1 FY27.
- [Leadership] Founder Ashok Soota recognized in the AIM 100 under the Specialist Forces category; Preeti Menon recognized among the AIM Top 24 Women Enterprise AI Leaders in India.

American energy infrastructure company covering data platforms, pipelines and the Power BI/reporting estate.
